chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam from his father, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Indeed, he said: The Shia of Ali (peace be upon him) are the pale-faced, the thin, the withered, withering with a withering; their lips are dry, their stomachs are changed in color.'
ai.seo_question: What are the physical characteristics of the Shia of Ali according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Sifat al-Shia*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as) links physical asceticism—manifested as pallor, thinness, and dry lips—to the spiritual discipline of the true followers of Ali. This description reflects the historical context of the Ahl al-Bayt's community enduring hardship and voluntary poverty, serving as a visible sign of their detachment from worldly luxuries and their deep devotion. It establishes a theological framework where external humility mirrors internal piety, a key characteristic in Shia identity.

en.badr-shahin: My father, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated to us from Ahmed bin Idris from Mohammed bin Ahmed from Mohammed bin Easa from Abu Mohammed al-Ansari from Amr bin Abi al-Miqdam from his father that
Abu Ja’far (a) said to him: O Abu al-Miqdam, the Shia of Ali (a) are the pale, the thin, and the emaciated. Their lips are dry, their stomachs are atrophied, and their colors are faded.
